title: CORS Reflects Any Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (incl. null origin)
description: The Azure Container Apps backend reflects any arbitrary Origin header verbatim with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, confirmed for attacker-controlled domains and the null origin. This allows any attacker-controlled web page (including sandboxed iframes) to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read authenticated API responses, enabling cross-origin session and token theft.
evidence_safe: HTTP 200 on /health with Origin:https://attacker.com returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin:https://attacker.com + Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true. Origin:null also reflected.
evidence_quarantined:
Request: curl -H 'Origin: https://attacker.com' https://revops-dev.livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io/health
Response headers: access-control-allow-origin: https://attacker.com
access-control-allow-credentials: true
access-control-allow-methods: GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE,OPTIONS
access-control-allow-headers: Content-Type,Authorization

Origin: null also reflected with credentials: true

title: Post-Auth SSRF Candidate: URL-Accepting Parameters May Reach Azure IMDS
description: The backend exposes URL-accepting parameters (url, redirect, target, proxy, callback, webhook) on /api that return HTTP 401 when unauthenticated. If authentication is bypassed via the CORS+nonce chain, these parameters could be used to proxy requests to the Azure IMDS endpoint (http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token) to retrieve managed identity access tokens for Azure resource pivot.
evidence_safe: All /api?<param>=<IMDS-URL> returned HTTP 401 unauthenticated. Parameters url/redirect/target/proxy/callback/webhook confirmed to exist and gate on auth.
evidence_quarantined:
curl /api?url=http%3A%2F%2F169.254.169.254%2Fmetadata%2Finstance... -> HTTP 401 {"error":"Unauthorized: no valid token"}
Same for redirect, target, proxy, callback, webhook params. Auth required before SSRF test can confirm reachability.

title: Azure Container Apps Environment ID Exposed in FQDN Enabling Sibling Enumeration
description: The Container Apps environment name 'livelystone-c1480484' is embedded in the application FQDN. Probing 9 common sibling app name patterns confirmed the environment is live and routable (all returned Azure platform 404s, not DNS NXDOMAIN). No additional sibling apps were found active in this scan, but the environment ID enables targeted future enumeration.
evidence_safe: 9 sibling app names probed under livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io. All returned HTTP 404 Azure platform page (not NXDOMAIN). Environment confirmed live.
evidence_quarantined: HTTP/2 404 with Azure Container App Unavailable page for: revops, revops-api, revops-worker, revops-prod, api, backend, worker, scheduler, admin. Environment resolves confirming livelystone-c1480484 is an active ACA environment.
